name: Post Hoc
aliases: After this, therefore because of this
shortDef: Assuming that because B followed A, A must have caused B.
definition: Concluding that one event caused another simply because it came first. Timing alone can't rule out coincidence, a shared cause, or a change that would have happened anyway, like a cold clearing up on its own.
howToSpot: Is the only evidence that one thing happened right after another?
Would the outcome have happened anyway, through recovery, seasons or a bounce back?
Did anything else change around the same time?
classicExample: I started wearing my lucky socks on Monday and we've won every game since. The socks are working.
legitimateVersion: Timing is a fair first clue. It becomes good evidence when the effect repeats, appears and disappears with the suspected cause, or holds up against a comparison group.

contrast.fal_false_cause: Post hoc relies on one thing following another in time; false cause relies on two things going together across many cases.
contrast.fal_anecdotal_evidence: Post hoc infers cause from timing; anecdotal evidence lets a personal story outweigh broader data, whatever the timing.
